extracted.intended_audience: students (undergraduate/graduate) and instructors of mathematical logic / model theory
extracted.subtask_description: Precise rules and standards for interpreting first-order languages in structures: how terms are evaluated, how satisfaction/truth is defined, logical implication/validity, definability of relations, elementary classes, and homomorphisms/isomorphisms and their preservation properties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of variable assignment to terms (evaluation of terms)
rubrics_metrics.description: Define s : T → |A| (extension of s : V → |A|) by recursion: (1) for each variable x, s(x) = s(x); (2) for each constant symbol c, s(c) = c^A; (3) if t1,...,tn are terms and f is an n-place function symbol, then s(f t1 ... tn) = f^A(s(t1),...,s(tn)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The extension exists uniquely by the recursion theorem and uses unique decompositions of terms. s(t) is the element of |A| named by the term t; notation t^A[s] or s(t) may display dependence on A and s. Examples: s(f f v3)=S(S(2)) etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Satisfaction of atomic formulas: equality
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equality is treated as a logical symbol (not a parameter); this clause grounds all equality reasoning in semantics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Satisfaction of atomic formulas: predicate symbols
rubrics_metrics.description: |=A P t1 ... tn [s] iff (s(t1),...,s(tn)) ∈ P^A for an n-place predicate parameter P.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Atomic satisfaction is explicit (not recursive). Examples illustrate checking membership in the relation assigned to P in the structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recursive clauses for satisfaction of compound wffs
rubrics_metrics.description: For wffs ϕ, ψ: (1) |=A ¬ϕ[s] iff not |=A ϕ[s]; (2) |=A (ϕ → ψ)[s] iff either not |=A ϕ[s] or |=A ψ[s] (i.e., standard material implication); (3) |=A ∀x ϕ[s] iff for every d ∈ |A|, |=A ϕ[s(x|d)].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The clause for ∃ is given via ¬∀¬ equivalence: |=A ∃x α[s] iff there exists d ∈ |A| with |=A α[s(x|d)]. Conjunction/disjunction/↔ are handled by standard abbreviations. Use s(x|d) to denote s modified at x.

rubrics_metrics.name: Satisfaction depends only on values at free variables (Theorem 22A)
rubrics_metrics.description: If s1 and s2 are assignments that agree on all variables free in ϕ, then |=A ϕ[s1] iff |=A ϕ[s2].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof by induction on ϕ using the recursive satisfaction clauses. Justifies notation that for a sentence s is irrelevant and that only the values for free variables matter for non-sentences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sentences: truth in a structure (Corollary 22B)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a sentence σ, either (a) A satisfies σ with every function s : V → |A|, or (b) A satisfies σ with no such s. If (a) holds we write |=A σ and say σ is true in A (A is a model of σ); otherwise σ is false in A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This follows from Theorem 22A because sentences have no free variables. A is a model of a set Σ of sentences iff it is a model of every member of Σ.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notation for satisfaction with parameters: |=A ϕ[[a1,...,ak]]
rubrics_metrics.description: If all free variables of ϕ are among v1,...,vk then |=A ϕ[[a1,...,ak]] means A satisfies ϕ with any assignment s for which s(vi)=ai for 1≤i≤k.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This shorthand is used throughout examples (e.g., |=N ∀v2 P v1 v2 [[0]]). It relies on Theorem 22A to ensure independence of the rest of s.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of logical implication (Γ |= φ)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a set Γ of wffs and wff φ, Γ logically implies φ (Γ |= φ) iff for every structure A and every assignment s : V → |A|, if A satisfies every member of Γ with s then A satisfies φ with s.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Same symbol |= used earlier for satisfaction; for sentences, Γ |= τ equivalently means every model of Γ is a model of τ. Logical equivalence: φ ≡ ψ iff φ |= ψ and ψ |= φ.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validity
rubrics_metrics.description: A wff ϕ is valid iff ∅ |= ϕ (written simply |= ϕ); equivalently ϕ is true in every structure under every assignment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Validity is the first-order analogue of a tautology. Determining validity requires quantifying over all structures and assignments, which makes decidability fail in general (though validities are effectively enumerable via completeness/deduction results discussed later).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definability of relations in a structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Given structure A and a formula ϕ whose free variables are among v1,...,vk, the k-ary relation defined by ϕ in A is {(a1,...,ak) | |=A ϕ[[a1,...,ak]]}. A k-ary relation on |A| is definable in A iff some formula (with appropriate free variables) defines it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: in (R;0,1,+,·) the nonnegative reals [0,∞) are defined by ∃v2 v1 = v2·v2; ordering is definable by ∃v3 v2 = v1 + v3·v3. Some sets (e.g., singletons {n} in N) are definable; many others are not (uncountably many relations but only countably many formulas). Complexity of definability may be measured by complexity of simplest defining formula.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elementary class / EC notion
rubrics_metrics.description: A class K of structures is elementary (EC) iff K = Mod τ for some sentence τ; K is EC (wider sense) iff K = Mod Σ for some set Σ of sentences. Mod Σ denotes the class of all models of Σ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: class of all graphs, groups, fields are elementary; class of finite graphs is not elementary. Some classes are EC (by infinite sets of sentences), e.g., inﬁnite groups as Mod{group_axioms ∪ {there are at least n things for each n}}.

rubrics_metrics.name: Homomorphism and isomorphism (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: A homomorphism h : |A| → |B| satisfies (a) for each n-place predicate parameter P and tuple (a1,...,an): (a1,...,an) ∈ P^A iff (h(a1),...,h(an)) ∈ P^B; (b) for each n-place function symbol f and tuple (a1,...,an): h(f^A(a1,...,an)) = f^B(h(a1),...,h(an)); and for constants c: h(c^A)=c^B. If h is one-to-one it is an isomorphism (embedding); if onto and isomorphism then A ≅ B.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some authors use weaker homomorphisms; these are strong homomorphisms. Substructure characterization: A is a substructure of B iff |A|⊆|B| and each predicate/function/constant of A is the restriction of the corresponding one in B (closure under functions required).

rubrics_metrics.name: Homomorphism theorem (preservation results)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let h be a homomorphism A→B and s an assignment into |A|. (a) For any term t, h(s(t)) = (h◦s)(t). (b) For any quantifier-free formula α not containing equality, |=A α[s] iff |=B α[h◦s]. (c) If h is one-to-one, the equivalence in (b) holds also for formulas with equality. (d) If h is onto, the equivalence in (b) extends to formulas with quantifiers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proofs use induction on terms/formulas. Consequences: homomorphisms preserve truth of quantifier-free formulas (and more under injectivity/surjectivity). Useful to relate substructures, embeddings, and preservation of properties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Isomorphism implies elementary equivalence (Corollary 22D)
rubrics_metrics.description: If A ≅ B then A ≡ B, i.e., isomorphic structures satisfy exactly the same first-order sentences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stronger fact: isomorphic structures agree on higher-order sentences too. There exist elementarily equivalent but non-isomorphic structures (e.g., (Q,<) and (R,<)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Automorphisms preserve definable relations (Corollary 22E)
rubrics_metrics.description: If h is an automorphism of A and R is an n-ary relation definable in A, then for all a1,...,an ∈ |A|: (a1,...,an) ∈ R iff (h(a1),...,h(an)) ∈ R.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Take a formula ϕ that defines R; apply the homomorphism theorem to conclude the equivalence. This is a standard tool to show certain sets are not definable (e.g., N is not definable in (R,<) because increasing automorphisms can map N outside N).

rubrics_metrics.name: Observations about complexity of validity and decidability
rubrics_metrics.description: Determining whether a first-order wff is valid requires considering every structure A and every assignment s, including infinite universes, so validity is considerably more complex than sentential tautology; as a consequence the set of valid first-order formulas is not decidable, though it is effectively enumerable via completeness (deducibility) results to be developed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text emphasizes the contrast with propositional logic where tautologies are decidable by finite truth tables; points forward to Section 2.4 and later results (completeness, enumerability).
